jobs.description: Work Flexibility: Onsite It's Time to Join Stryker! In this role, you will serve as a systems engineering owner for robotic end effectors , including powered surgical tools and future attachments that interface directly with the robotic system. You will help translate user and clinical needs into system architecture and requirements, define interfaces across electrical, mechanical, and software disciplines, and guide the product from requirements development through integration and verification. This role requires a highly collaborative engineer who can bring together input from multiple technical disciplines and maintain a system-level view throughout development. Translate user, clinical, and product needs into clear, verifiable system requirements and design inputs. Develop and refine system architectures, interfaces, and functional requirements across electrical, mechanical, software, and controls disciplines. Allocate and decompose system requirements to appropriate subsystems and engineering disciplines. Lead technical trade studies, design assessments, performance analyses, and other systems engineering activities used to guide design decisions. Support concept development and architecture definition for new end effectors, features, and product capabilities. Requirements, Integration, and Verification Establish and maintain requirements traceability throughout the product development lifecycle. Develop system-level verification strategies and ensure requirements can be objectively verified. Lead system integration activities across multiple engineering disciplines. Investigate and help resolve complex system-level design and integration issues. Lead or support system verification and validation activities as development progresses. Contribute to product risk management and ensure appropriate linkage between risks, requirements, mitigations, and verification evidence. Create and maintain engineering documentation supporting the Design History File. Cross-Functional Leadership Collaborate with Electrical, Mechanical, Software, Systems, Clinical, Quality, Regulatory, Manufacturing, and other stakeholders to ensure successful system development. Support Voice of Customer activities and translate clinical workflows and customer needs into actionable engineering inputs. Mentor engineers in systems engineering, requirements development, design controls, risk management, and verification practices. Identify and implement improvements to systems engineering processes, tools, and practices. What You Will Need Minimum Qualifications Bachelor of Science degree in Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. 4+ years of applicable engineering experience. Preferred Qualifications Experience developing or managing system requirements for complex products. Experience working across multiple engineering disciplines such as electrical, mechanical, software, systems, or test. Experience developing medical devices or other complex regulated products. Experience with systems architecture, requirements development, decomposition, interface definition, integration, and verification. Experience translating user or customer needs into system-level design inputs and requirements. Experience developing verification strategies and supporting system integration and testing. Experience with robotic systems, powered surgical tools, power tools, or other precision electromechanical products. Experience with requirements management tools such as Jama, IBM DOORS, or equivalent. Working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, design controls, and medical device development practices. INCOSE CSEP certification or equivalent systems engineering certification. Strong communication and relationship-building skills with the ability to influence across technical disciplines. $102,600 - $171,000 USD Annual Travel Percentage: 10% Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role
As a Channel Partner Manager for Korea, you will be responsible for building, managing, and scaling strategic partnerships with both System Integrators (SIs) and resellers to accelerate the adoption of our solutions in the Korean market. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and Korea's unique business ecosystem, helping partners integrate our products into their solution portfolios and joint go-to-market strategies.
As a Channel Partner Manager, you will focus on growing the partner Anthropic reseller and services business in Korea and achieving quarterly revenue and partner attach targets through new customers and upsells. You'll be the local owner of these partner relationships in Korea. Our partners will look to you for everything that makes the channel work day to day from initial onboarding to deal registration, enablement, billing and contracting questions, escalations. Our internal teams will look to you for what is happening in the market, how partners are driving new opportunities and growth within existing customers. You'll work closely with the local sales team and the central program team, co-selling on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities and managing direct versus partner conflict as deals arise. Strong business creation skills are needed to identify joint value propositions and explore co-selling models. Much of the process for running the channel in Korea doesn't exist yet, and building it will be a large part of the job in the first year. While revenue contribution is the key metric, building scalable partner engagement and executing joint initiatives are crucial for consistent growth.
This is an early role in a new market for a program we expect to grow well beyond its first two countries. The habits you establish with our first partners in Korea will shape how the program works everywhere else.
Key responsibilities
Own the day-to-day relationships with Anthropic's strategic resellers and system integrators in Korea, acting as their primary local point of contact, including billing, contracting and general queries
Own deal registration and pipeline discipline with partners, making sure registrations are submitted and validated, conflicts are cleared, and named end-customer reporting is complete on every deal
Forecast and report partner pipeline and performance against the quarterly revenue and partner attach targets, and own the Korea channel number with the central program team
Negotiate resale agreements and commercial terms with partners alongside the central program team and Legal
Co-sell with the local account team on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, and manage direct versus partner conflict as deals arise

We are challenged with an important job to safely find and deliver energy to the world. Our employees are critical to our success, and with them we power civilization. We’re grounded by our SPIRIT Values – safety, people, integrity, responsibility, innovation, and teamwork. Job Summary ConocoPhillips holds approximately 782,000 unconventional net acres in the Delaware Basin, spanning west Texas through southeast New Mexico. Current development activity targets prospects in the Avalon, Bone Springs, Wolfcamp and Woodford formations while balancing leasehold obligations and permit terms. We operated ten rigs and three frac crews on average during 2025, resulting in 176 operated wells drilled and 161 operated wells brought online. During 2025, net production averaged 661 MBOED. Position Overview As an Automation Technician in Loving, NM , you will support safe, reliable field operations by maintaining and troubleshooting automation, instrumentation, and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. You will work closely with operations, engineering, vendors, and contractors to resolve issues, support new installations, and reduce repeat failures. Your work directly supports operational uptime, safety performance, and environmental protection. This role offers hands-on technical experience in field automation, exposure to evolving technologies, and opportunities to grow technical depth and broaden responsibility within a collaborative team environment. Your responsibilities may include: Perform all work in alignment with Department of Transportation (DOT), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), National Electrical Code (NEC), National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), and company safety requirements. Follow energy isolation and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures when working on automated and electrical equipment. Install, inspect, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot field automation, instrumentation, communications, and related electrical equipment. Diagnose SCADA, instrumentation, and control system issues and restore safe, reliable operation in a timely manner. Execute preventive and predictive maintenance activities and complete required documentation accurately and on time. Support Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) installation, troubleshooting, and programming updates. Assist with commissioning of new equipment and facilities, including loop checks, logic testing, and SCADA verification. Create, update, and close maintenance work orders and notifications using the maintenance management system. Maintain accurate technical documentation, including maintenance records, prints, and project documentation. Identify recurring issues, communicate findings, and support root cause analysis to prevent repeat failures. Initiate Management of Change (MOC) requests for equipment, instrumentation, or program changes. Collaborate with operations, engineering, and peers to improve reliability, safety, and cost effectiveness. Success Profile To thrive in this role, you’ll demonstrate the following leadership competencies: Takes Accountability: Takes ownership of actions and follows through on commitments by courageously dealing with important problems, holding others accountable, and standing up for what is right. Drives Performance: Delivers results through realistic planning to accomplish goals. Makes Decisions: Generates effective solutions based on available information and makes timely decisions that are safe and ethical. Qualifications: Basic Requirements Legally authorized to work in the United States. Current/valid driver's license. 3 or more years of experience in automation, instrumentation, controls, SCADA support, or related field operations. Working knowledge of maintaining and troubleshooting field automation and instrumentation equipment. Are you able to perform the physical demands and work environment requirements of the position, as described in the job description, with or without reasonable accommodation? Preferred Requirement Associate degree, trade certificate, or higher in Instrumentation, Electronics, Electrical Technology, or equivalent. 5 or more years of experience in the automation field. Experience with PLCs, Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), and automation platforms such as Allen-Bradley, Emerson ROC, ABB, SCADAPack, or similar systems. Experience with field communications equipment such as cellular modems, radios, and network switches. Knowledge of electrical systems, National Electrical Code, and safe work practices. Ability to read and apply control narratives, cause-and-effect documentation, Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) concepts, and Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs). Strong troubleshooting skills and ability to communicate technical findings clearly. Physical Demands & Work Environment This is a Safety Sensitive position. The position is based in Loving, NM and includes regular travel to wellsites and facilities, with up to 10% travel annually. Work requires climbing ladders and stairs up to 50 feet to access equipment. Work requires lifting, carrying, and transporting items weighing up to 50 pounds. Daily work includes walking, standing, stooping, sitting, climbing, and carrying materials on even and uneven terrain. Work is performed outdoors in harsh weather conditions and frequently involves working independently for extended periods. Required personal protective equipment (PPE) must be worn in accordance with site and task requirements. The position is a Monday-Friday schedule and requires rotating on-call weekend responsibilities, emergency response, and flexibility to work unscheduled overtime. Apply By: Oct 11, 2026 Sponsorship: ConocoPhillips’ sponsorship for employment authorization in the U.S. is NOT available for this position. Benefits Overview ConocoPhillips offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and career growth: Taking Care of Your Health & Wellness : Medical, dental, vision, mental health support, and wellness programs. Supporting and Building Financial Security : Competitive base pay, annual performance bonuses, and retirement savings plans. Promoting Work-Life Balance : Paid time off, paid parental leave, and family support resources. Offering Career Development : Access to training, mentoring, and internal career mobility tools. Guiding Recognition & Inclusion : Peer-nominated awards, inclusive culture, and employee resource groups. Why ConocoPhillips At ConocoPhillips, we believe our people power the future of energy. We’re committed to creating a workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow—professionally and personally. We don’t just offer jobs—we offer meaningful careers in a company that values how we work as much as what we achieve. EEO: In the US, ConocoPhillips is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About this Role:
This is your chance to have a critical impact at a dynamic gaming company in the midst of an exciting globalization journey. You'll be joining the Group International Legal Department which oversees legal matters for the NetEase group and coordinates with the legal teams within each division of the group.
We are looking for a talented Group Transactional and Commercial Counsel. In this leadership role, you will be advising on a dynamic range of M&A, investments and divestments across multiple jurisdictions, and technology, media and telecom and general commercial matters at the highest international standards, including licensing, outsourcing, software technology development and professional services agreements, innovative FinTech projects, regulatory matters and cross-border technology transfers.
This position will report to the General Counsel of NetEase, Inc.
NetEase operates in multiple countries globally, and this role is primarily responsible for:
Corporate Transactions
Lead deal execution on a wide range of corporate transactions, including structuring, drafting, and negotiating transaction documents for acquisitions, disposals, minority investments, fund investments, financing transactions and joint ventures across multiple jurisdictions.
Assess and advise senior stakeholders on legal, regulatory, and commercial risks relating to corporate transactions.
Navigate regulatory approvals including antitrust, foreign investment clearances, and securities law requirements across multiple jurisdictions.
Work with legal team to provide end-to-end transaction support, including structuring, due diligence, drafting, negotiation, and completion.
Coordinate closely with internal business teams (e.g., senior management of business units and the NetEase group, business development, finance, tax, etc.) on all aspects of transactions.
Provide legal support on post-transaction monitoring and corporate governance matters.
Commercial Contract Management & TMT Advisory
Draft, review, and negotiate a variety of TMT and other commercial agreements for the NetEase group and individual business units across multiple jurisdictions.
Provide thought leadership regarding the legal and regulatory aspects of projects involving cutting-edge technologies such as Web3, blockchain, AI, tokenization, online payment systems, AI, etc.
Advise on TMT related policies and procedures, including terms of use and custody and trust arrangements.
Keep up-to-date with the most recent technology legal and business developments and continue to develop relevant knowledge within the sectors in which the NetEase group operates.
Support NetEase group's corporate functions (finance, tax, procurement, IT, corporate secretarial, corporate M&A/ JV, global investments, HR, treasury and others), including daily contract reviews, in-house advisory and commercial disputes.
Establish contract standards and templates to streamline the review process for everyday commercial agreements across business units.
Core Competencies
Lead and mentor a high-performing team of legal counsel, fostering a collaborative, business-oriented legal culture, and work closely with other legal specialists within the NetEase group.
Provide training to the wider legal & internal control functions, business partners and executive leadership.
Select, manage and coordinate external counsel and advisors across different jurisdictions to ensure high-quality, cost-effective representation.
Ability to bridge international deals using high-level Mandarin and English language skills to review and negotiate bilingual transaction and commercial documents.
Qualifications:
Admitted and licensed attorney in U.S., Hong Kong, Singapore or another major common-law jurisdiction with 8+ years relevant post-qualification experience working in well-regarded law firms and/or in-house legal teams; in-house experience preferred.
Ability to lead, manage and motivate team members located in multiple jurisdictions.
Self-starter and able to navigate various stakeholders/ businesses operating in different sectors and jurisdictions.
Excellent transactional training.
Expertise with TMT laws, regulations and industry best practices across different regions, including an understanding of emerging trends such as in the areas of FinTech/blockchain, money transmission, AI, online game regulation and digital infrastructure.
Strong drafting, negotiating and problem-solving skills and the ability to manage complex issues and deal structures.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the flexibility and cultural sensitivity to bring different perspectives together and work through competing priorities.
Demonstrated leadership abilities, including the ability to influence and drive change within the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make informed decisions in complex situations.
Experienced in managing outside counsel.
Comfortable working with a geographically dispersed team.
High-level proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and English is a must.
Preferred Location:
Hong Kong, Singapore or another Asia-Pacific hub; U.S., Canada or other locations considered for exceptional candidates.

At NetEase, we are committed to fair employment practices. We welcome applications from all individuals, irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.
